MEASURED on this live journey (39 nodes, three runs each, `ann serve` on 127.0.0.1): BEFORE GET /api/whatsnext 3.523 / 3.500 / 3.476s (every other read 0.0057-0.0068s); AFTER 0.0162 / 0.0065 / 0.0069s — GET /api/journey over the same runs 0.0061 / 0.0058 / 0.0057s, so the read is back in the other reads' class. Pinned deterministically, not by the clock: src/surface/__tests__/whatsnext-read.test.ts mocks the pre-check's module and asserts whatsNext() calls it ZERO times on a clean AND on a dirty tree, while integritySnapshot() calls it exactly once; src/e2e/whats-next.e2e.test.ts adds the latency-class bound (<1000ms) that a re-regressed read cannot pass.

The write guard did not move: operatorIntegrityBlockers() and runOperatorAction() are untouched, the approve still re-checks integrity FIRST and fail-closed with the named blockers, and the drive path is unchanged — the existing approve tests pass as they were (src/surface/__tests__/approve.test.ts care a/b + the in-process approve tests: a dirty tree refuses refused-integrity with zero writes; a clean one runs the frame). DISPLAY DECISION (recorded, option b): the card's read returns integrity {state:'unchecked', note} and the page fetches the verdict LAZILY from the new GET /api/integrity, which serves the SAME operatorIntegrityBlockers — so the displayed verdict and the write's refusal cannot drift. The page shows CHECKING INTEGRITY + a 'not run on load' fact while in flight, then the real clean/dirty result; a dirty tree shows BLOCKED - CANNOT ADVANCE with its named blockers (never a stale or blank claim), and an unreadable snapshot says INTEGRITY UNKNOWN and still offers the approve, because the write's own re-check decides. Pinned by src/surface/__tests__/ui-drill.test.ts (pending/clean/dirty renderings) and the e2e's GET /api/integrity round trips.

The page renders BEFORE the verdict: refresh() renders the card from the fast reads and calls loadIntegrity() afterwards, so a load never blocks on the pre-check; while it is in flight the badge reads CHECKING INTEGRITY, the integrity fact says the pre-check is not run on load, and no approve is shown — then the answer lands and the card re-renders with it (a superseded read is dropped by its generation counter, never displayed). The earlier invariants hold: no approve where it cannot work (boundary derivation, pending or dirty verdict, no ready task), the boundary/dirty/blocked words are unchanged, and every blocker is still a drill. Pinned by the new ui-drill test 'THE PAGE RENDERS BEFORE THE INTEGRITY VERDICT' (the fetch is held open), plus the existing boundary / empty-chain / hidden-guard / exhausted-journey tests, which run unchanged.
